explanation: It took its name from the town but was held on Max Yasgur's dairy farm near Bethel, New York, about 70 km (43 miles) southwest of Woodstock.

claims.text: The 1969 Woodstock festival was held near Bethel, New York, more than 50 km from the town of Woodstock.
The Woodstock festival was named after the town of Woodstock, New York.
The festival site on Max Yasgur's dairy farm near Bethel lies about 70 km (43 miles) southwest of the town of Woodstock.
43 miles is about 69 km, which rounds to about 70 km.

writerNotes: Self-check (§9.3). Lint: clean under content:check for writer w-pmusic02w. Claims: every checkable statement in the statement and explanation is listed, with risk at or above the C26 floor and raised where a fact is beyond everyday knowledge. Datasets: geonames-cities lists Woodstock, New York (US, admin1 NY, 42.04092, -74.1182), but has no record for Bethel, New York, so the distance needs web evidence; c4 is a pure conversion (43 x 1.609344 = 69.2), which a calculation confirms. I used no WebSearch. Rival test: argued for 'false': the name makes nearly everyone assume the festival was in Woodstock. Argued against the key: the farm near Bethel is about 43 miles (69 km) from Woodstock, so the bounded 50 km claim holds with a wide margin, whatever exact route or measure is used. Volatility: evergreen; no time words, and nothing depends on knowledge newer than mid-2026. Regional: Woodstock is famous worldwide as a festival name, and the stem gives the distance in kilometres. Style: Oxford spelling, straight quotes, no en or em dashes, explanation within 35 words. Myths: screened against content/reference/myths.json, no hit. Mystery: not applicable to a practice item. Encore: not applicable to a practice item. Doubts: The exact distance depends on the measure (straight line or road); the stem uses the bounded claim on purpose and the explanation says 'about'.
